newsitem.title: UK: Partners key in managing risk - Goldman Sachs.
newsitem.headline: Partners key in managing risk - Goldman Sachs.

text.p: One of the best ways to manage market risk is to have partners actively involved on the trading floor, said a risk managment official at the U.S.-based investment bank Goldman Sachs International.
Traders, and partners with their capital at stake, are at the front line of Goldman Sachs' risk management strategy, said Bernard Minsky, executive director of firm-wide risk at Goldman.
And while value-at-risk (VAR) models are also a key part of risk management, they can not themselves prevent financial disasters, Minsky told a conference on risk models in London.
"The front line of risk management is the traders," he said.
"We also have partners on the floor," he said. "It's their capital at risk. We find this very powerful in terms of control of the business."
VAR models measure the potential loss in the market value of a portfolio using mathematical equations that measure variables such as volatility.

VAR and stress testing, which tests a firm's risk profile under extreme conditions and gives worst case scenarios, have become popular tools in determining how much risk financial institutions are exposed to.
Minsky said VAR is used across the company's business lines, like equities, fixed income, currencies and commodities, rather than across separate business entities.
He said Goldman now has risk committees meeting once a week, as well as a separate risk group carrying out more intensive analytical work using specific models.
He said the "Linear Value at Risk" model was the group's main risk model. While it has its roots in fixed income, it can be aggregated across different sectors.
Goldman uses this model regularly to look at "hot spots", where it has a large exposure to a specific market. The model is available to the risk management group and traders, he said.
Minsky said in commodities and currencies, historic simulation models were useful, while stress testing is used actively in equities.
"Particularly in equities, traders like to use this a great deal," he said.
But Minsky said all models must be treated with caution and only as part of a firm' overall risk management strategy. Goldman also views holding periods as important, he said.
"VAR, stress testing, capital at risk, are not the answer," Minsky said. "There is a danger in having a model-generated measure of VAR if you think it is the be-all-and-end-all."
He added: "We are also aware unexpected events happen more than you would expect."
